q: How do I split a chemical plant's emissions between its products?
title: Allocating emissions in a multi-product plant
short: Measure what you can per product, such as dedicated reactors or steam lines, then split the shared energy by a stated rule, such as mass of output, or batch hours when products need very different heating. Keep the rule the same each year and state it with every product figure.
audience: Chemical, dye and pharma plants making several products in one facility

ul: Direct measurement: sub-meters or steam meters per line.
Physical allocation: kilograms of output or reactor hours.
Economic allocation by revenue, only when physical rules do not fit.

p: Mass allocation gives every kilogram the same share, even if one product needs twice the heating. If heating time differs a lot, reactor hours or steam per batch give a fairer split.
Give the per-kilogram figure, the rule used and the share of energy that was directly metered, so the buyer can judge how close the number is to the product.

example.title: Worked example: mass allocation (one month, illustrative inputs)
lines: Plant total: 104,100 kg CO2 for 500 t of output
Per kg, either product: 104,100 / 500,000 = 0.208 kg CO2
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; ISO 14067 and the GHG Protocol Product Standard set the allocation order.
